questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to experience living in a big city, and go outside of Europe. Furthermore, I thought it was a bonus, that English was an official language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is really an amazing experience to live and study abroad. You learn to build a life for yourself in another city and get a whole new perspective on your life in Denmark. However, it can also be quite hard and feel a little lonely at times, but you just have to lean into it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: You can just do research on the UofT website, and if you need more information you can always call or email the office or professors of specific courses. UofT also host some zoom-meetings for incoming exchange students with information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When I first arrived at the airport, there was a booth with UofT students. They gave you maps of the campus and information. In the days around school start, there are also plenty of booths around campus handing out different flyers and information, and UofT host an information meeting in the first week of classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: UofT didn't really do anything to get the exchange students together socially, so you had to do that on your own initiative. Furthermore, there were no tours of campus, so before school starts, you should check out where your courses are, and do your own little orientation tour of the campus to find the right buildings and rooms.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I started my househunt (end July) quite late and found something called campus-coop. I would definitely recommend everyone to stay in campus-coop, as it is very cheap (I had the cheapest rent of anyone I met in Toronto), and you live close to campus. In campus-coop you have to make an application, but I think it's quite easy to get in as a danish exchange student. You then have your own room but share a house with other students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend living Downton (between dupont st, dufferin st & Parliament st). Public transportation in Toronto can be quite bad, slow and late, so it's nice to be able to live close to campus, and also be mobile and flexible when you want to hang out with your friends, who will most likely also be living around campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UofT dies not offer housing for students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to apply for courses through a google sheet in end may/start June. It is really important that you list all the courses you've already taken at UCPH, otherwise you won't get in. If you don't get in to enough courses you have to try again in the 2nd round, and then apply for courses with available spots.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can just do research on the website, or call/email the office or professors. After arrival you can also show top at the offices for late registry.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: First I applied for 5 courses and got in to 4. I then dropped one, and applied for another two in the 2nd round. I got into both of them and then dropped one of them later. I think in general, they are pretty nice at letting exchange students into courses, and if you are not sure, it would be a good idea to email the professor of the specific course before registration starts, to ask if you can join their course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can apply for a maximum of 5 courses. even though you only need four, it's a good idea to apply for 5 just to be sure, and then you can always just drop one course. -And also email the professors for help and information. A lot of them are helpfull.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 300-level courses and 1 400-level course. However, I think the difficulty of a course depends more on the subject and the professor than on the actual level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is a bit more like high school. You have to show up to class and actively participate, as this will most likely affect your grades. This also means that the other student are way more active in class than at UCPH. Furthermore, the workload throughout the term is also bigger, due to assignments etc that will affect your final grade. However, the content of the work is a bit easier, as it is not as theoretical as at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POL301H1 Colonial legacies and post-independence African Politics (valgfag)
POL380H1 Topics in international politics: Gender and intersectionality in Global Politics (Valgfag)
POL378H1 Topics in Comparative Politics: Law and Political Development (DAK3)
EUR498H1 Special Topics in European affairs: European Union (EP)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It really depends on what you're into. I really like critical theory and therefore chose courses about post colonialism and intersectionalism, as UofT offers a broad range of courses on critical theory and diversity. However, you can take courses within almost every faculty, so it is also a great opportunity to explore new fields such as media, law, history etc. As for the style of studying, you won't really know if it works for you, until you've tried it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: All international students in Toronto are obliged to pay for a health insurance called UHIP. It's around 1200 dkk and then you can go to the hospital and doctor for free without any worry or hassle, if an accident happens. It's really nice.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The only thing that's cheaper in Toronto compared to Denmark is to-go coffee and 2nd hand stores. Groceries and alcohol is quite expensive, but you can get some relatively cheap meals, when you eat out actually.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the clubs are related to race or religion (black lawyers of tomorrow or future muslim doctors eg.)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of sport teams. Some of them require try-outs and some of them has a fee. However, there are a lot of sportfacilities around campus that all students can use for free. I my self swam three times a week, but you can also go ice skating, play tennis, basket or squat with your friends completely free. There are also a lot of clubs. In the weekend before school starts, there's a clubs fair, where you can walk around and see if there's something for you. A lot of clubs, you don't even have to be a part of to show up to their events. it's just all about following the right instagrams and mailing lists to know what going on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definetly go see some uni-sports games!! It's completely free for students and a good way to get some school spirit. The center for international experience also regularly hosts get togethers where you can meet fellow international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you have the time (eg. during reading week) definetly go to Banff! It's really beautiful. I also went to Montreal and really loved it. There are lot of great places and cities in Ontario and the east of Canada, that you can reach in a few hours with bus or a rented car. If you go to Algonquin, try to go in the middle of October to see the beutifull colors of the leafs just before they fall off.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. It's basically what you expect from watching american movies.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with them. That's what I did, and it was really nice. Otherwise, just talk to them in classes. People don't talk much to each other in classes, but I promise you, if you start a conversation, they will be very nice and welcoming.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching and the way the school work was probably the most different, but also the poverty rates. There's a lot of homelessness in Toronto, but I did not feel unsafe at any point.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Canadian people are definetly the most nice and welcoming people I have ever met, and you will smalltalk a lot with strangers. Also, the fact that Toronto is too international and multicultural. It literally feels like the whole world is gathered in one place, which also means that there isn't really one specific local culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live at campus coop
Say yes to everything
Don't be afraid to take initiative and write in the exchange group chats. Everybody just wants to meet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many new friends, and getting a whole new perspective on my life in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from everyone I know and love. At first it is really hard that every time you go out, it's almost like 'friend-dating' and getting to know people, and you don't really have anyone who really knows you, but you'll get there, and it will be sooo fun in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
